interface.name: zwlr_virtual_pointer_manager_v1
interface.description:
The virtual pointer manager is a singleton global object that provides the ability to emulate pointer input.
The virtual pointer will produce events as if the input device is a real device, e.g. to trigger a screen scroll the client needs to send axis events with a source of finger followed by a frame.

request.name: create_virtual_pointer
request.description: Creates a new virtual pointer. Note that the pointer will only be usable once a seat is provided: the compositor may ignore virtual pointer objects without a bound seat.

request.name: create_virtual_pointer_with_output

description.summary: Create a new virtual pointer with an output

request.description: Creates a new virtual pointer associated with the given output. Scroll and motion events are delivered relative to that output.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the virtual pointer manager. Virtual pointers created from this manager are unaffected by destruction of the manager.

interface.name: zwlr_virtual_pointer_v1

enum.name: axis_source
enum.description: The values match wl_pointer.axis_source so compositors forward them unchanged.

request.name: motion
request.description: The pointer has moved from its previous position.

request.name: motion_absolute
request.description: The pointer has moved to an absolute position.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x-coordinate in the output's coordinate space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y-coordinate in the output's coordinate space

request.name: button
request.description: A button was pressed or released.

arg.name: button
arg.summary: the button that was pressed or released

request.name: axis
request.description: Scroll and other axis movement. The axis argument follows wl_pointer: 0 is vertical scroll, 1 is horizontal scroll.

arg.name: value
arg.summary: length of vector in surface coordinates

request.name: frame

description.summary: end of a pointer event sequence

request.description: Indicates the end of a set of events that logically belong together.

request.name: axis_source
request.description: Source information for the following axis events. Scrolling screenshots use the finger source so apps treat the scroll as a touch drag rather than a wheel tick.

request.name: axis_discrete
request.description: Discrete step information for scroll and other axes.

arg.name: value
arg.summary: length of vector in surface coordinates
